Aisha scraped dried semen off the Prophet's garment or washed it, and he prayed in it; menstrual blood on a garment is scraped, rubbed and rinsed before praying in it.
Passing two graves, the Prophet said their occupants were punished for carrying tales and carelessness about urine, and planted halves of a fresh twig on them hoping for relief.
The Prophet embraced and lay with his menstruating wives over a waist-wrapper or cloth, and called Umm Salama back under his cover when her menses began.
Menstruating Aisha combed and washed the Prophet's head during his I'tikaf and fetched him the mat; he drank and ate where she had, and recited Quran in her lap.
The Jews shunned menstruating women; after the verse on menstruation the Prophet permitted everything except intercourse, and his face changed when two companions proposed no contact like the Jews.
Ali, too shy to ask, sent al-Miqdad: prostatic fluid requires washing the organ and ablution; the Prophet, waking at night, relieved himself, washed face and hands and slept.
After intercourse the Prophet performed ablution before sleeping or eating, sometimes bathing first; one repeating intercourse should perform ablution, and he lay with his wives with a single bath.
Over Aisha's and Umm Salama's surprise, the Prophet told Umm Sulaim a woman seeing fluid after a sexual dream must bathe; it happens, as children resemble whichever parent's fluid prevails.
A Jewish rabbi asked the Prophet where people will be when the earth is changed, about Paradise's first food and drink and a child's sex, then declared him an Apostle.
Aisha and Maimuna describe the Prophet's bath after intercourse: washing hands and private parts, ablution as for prayer, water through hair roots and over the body, feet last, no towel.
The Prophet bathed from one vessel with Aisha, Maimuna or Umm Salama, using about a Sa' for bathing and a Mudd for ablution; Aisha showed the bath behind a curtain.
The Prophet poured three handfuls over his head and told Umm Salama she need not undo her plaits; Aisha faulted Ibn Amr for ordering women to undo theirs.
Asked how to bathe after menstruation, the Prophet taught the bath and a musk-scented piece of cotton for purifying; Aisha quietly explained it is applied to the traces of blood.
Fatimah b. Abu Hubaish and Umm Habiba, whose bleeding continued, were told it is a vein, not menstruation: leave prayer for the usual days, then bathe and pray.
Asking whether the questioner is a Haruriya, Aisha says menstruating women were told to make up missed fasts but not missed prayers.
Fatimah and Maimuna screened the Prophet while he bathed; a man must not look at another man's private parts nor a woman at a woman's, nor share one cover.
The Children of Israel bathed naked and taunted Moses, who bathed alone, until a stone ran off with his clothes and they saw he had no defect.
Carrying stones for the Ka'ba, the Prophet fainted on baring himself and was never seen naked again; he told Miswar not to walk naked, and sought cover when relieving himself.
Some reports require bathing only on emission, ablution sufficing otherwise; others, like Aisha's answer to Abu Musa, require it on intercourse itself; the Prophet abrogated some commands by others.
The Prophet ordered ablution after eating what fire has touched, yet he ate goat's shoulder, meat and roasted liver and then prayed without ablution.
The Prophet prayed after eating meat without ablution; ablution is due after camel meat, optional after mutton, and one in doubt leaves prayer only on a sound or smell.
Seeing a dead goat given in charity to Maimuna's freed slave-girl, the Prophet said only eating it is forbidden; tanning makes its skin pure, even skins brought by Magians.
Tayammum was revealed when Aisha's lost necklace stranded people waterless; Ammar learned wiping face and palms suffices; the Prophet wiped face and hands at a wall before returning a greeting.
Abu Huraira and Hudhaifa slipped away to bathe after meeting the Prophet while sexually defiled; he told them a believer is never defiled.
Aisha says the Prophet remembered Allah at all moments.
Coming out of the privy and offered food, the Prophet ate without ablution, saying he was not about to pray.
On entering the privy the Prophet sought refuge in Allah from wicked and noxious things.
The Prophet's whispered talk with a man delayed the prayer until the people dozed off; the Companions dozed and then prayed without performing ablution.
Seeking a way to announce prayer in Medina, Muslims proposed a bell, horn or fire; Bilal was told to call, doubling the Adhan's phrases and saying the Iqama's once.
Bilal and the blind Ibn Umm Maktum called the Adhan; the Prophet attacked at dawn only where he heard none, and said a goatherd calling it had left the Fire.
Those hearing the mu'adhdhin should repeat his words, then bless the Prophet and ask al-Wasila, a rank in Paradise, for him; such responses bring his intercession, forgiveness and Paradise.
At the call to prayer and the Iqama Satan flees, breaking wind, then returns to distract the worshipper until he does not know how much he has prayed.
The Prophet raised his hands to his shoulders or ears when beginning the prayer, before bowing and on rising from it, but not between the prostrations.
Abu Huraira said takbir at every bending and rising, calling his prayer the closest to the Prophet's, and Ali's prayer with takbir reminded Imran of the Prophet's.
Prayer without the Fatiha is not credited; Allah divides it between Himself and His servant verse by verse, and Abu Huraira says it suffices, though reciting more is better.
A man sent back three times to pray again was taught to perform ablution, face the Qibla, say takbir, recite, and bow, prostrate and sit calmly.
The Prophet felt a man reciting behind him was disputing his recitation; Anas never heard the Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar or Uthman recite Bismillah aloud.
Waking from a doze, the Prophet recited a newly revealed surah: al-Kauthar is a canal his Lord promised him, a cistern his people will reach, some turned away for innovating.
Wa'il saw the Prophet raise his hands, place right over left and prostrate between his palms; he taught the tashahhud like a surah, and Abu Musa relayed following the imam.
Asked how to bless him, the Prophet taught asking Allah to bless Muhammad and his family as He blessed Abraham's family; whoever blesses him once, Allah blesses ten times.
